thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert — Streaming timeouts for customer AcmeCorp (dedicated-vpc pool eu-west1). Multiple websocket sessions failing with 502/504 at the customer gateway. Suspected connection/idle timeout mismatch causing retries and duplicate backend sessions. Auto-escalate to on-call.

raj: seeing the alert. paging eng-oncall. tag @eng-oncall

eng-oncall: on it. pulling logs

eng-oncall: quick summary — client connections drop after ~65s, gateway returns 504, client retries immediately. downstream (redwood) shows streams established but client disconnects, KV cache kept alive causing session duplication. spikes in tokens/sec for Acme tenant, risk of noisy-neighboring cache thrash in dedicated pool.

eva: @raj @eng-oncall paging SRE mgr @mike as this is an enterprise VPC customer with mandated SLA.

raj: @julia (CSM) can you notify AcmeCorp engineering that we're investigating? ask them to hold off retries for now if possible.

julia (CSM): pinged them on call, they confirm their gateway (NGINX + custom gateway) has default keepalive 60s. they're willing to change configs if we provide guidance.

eng-oncall: evidence snippet:
```
2026-03-01T10:12:23Z INFO stream open tenant=acme session=abc123
2026-03-01T10:13:29Z WARN upstream timeout tenant=acme session=abc123 code=504 gateway=acme-gw-01
2026-03-01T10:13:29Z INFO client retry tenant=acme session=abc124
```

eng-oncall: reproduction steps indicate gateway idle timeout < our ping/keepalive cadence. client retries are immediate causing fresh sessions that hold KV cache duplicates.

raj: immediate mitigation options?

eva: propose three-tiered mitigations:
1) temporary routing change on Redwood side to force sticky sessions to same backend slot for Acme (prevent KV thrash)
2) request Acme to increase gateway keepalive to 300s and add application-level pings every 30s
3) add edge-level timeout override for Acme route (nginx upstream_timeout 600s) while we monitor

mike: agree. do 1 and 3 from our side ASAP. coordinate with Acme for 2.

eng-oncall: applying route change now.

eng-oncall: command run:
```
rctl route update --customer acme --set sticky=true --upstream-timeout=600 --pool dedicated-eu-west1 --reason "temp mitigation for gateway timeouts"
```

ops-bot: Route update accepted. Change ID: r-78431. Rolling to 3 edge nodes.

eng-oncall: rolling update done on edges. verifying sessions...

eng-oncall: metrics: 95th latency token generation stable, number of duplicate sessions per minute dropped from 18 to 1 for tenant acme. gateway 504s decreased.

julia (CSM): Acme applied keepalive increase on their test env to 300s and disabled immediate retry for 5xx. They will push to prod in 30m.

raj: great. notify customer-facing channel and update incident status. Postpone paging for now, monitor for 30m.

eva: I'll stay on until @mike confirms stable. @eng-oncall leave runbook notes. add follow-up: permanent configuration for VPC/dedicated customers to include keepalive guidance + route-level timeout defaults.

eng-oncall: added runbook entry under incident r-78431. snippet:
```
- If customer websocket disconnects at ~60-70s, advise gateway keepalive >=300s
- Add application ping every 30s
- Use sticky routing for sessions until gateway stable
- rctl route update --customer <org> --set sticky=true --upstream-timeout=<secs>
```

mike: oncall handoff in 20m — @raj you'll be handing to @eva? confirm

raj: I'm heading out in 15. handing to eva. eva takes over.

eva: taking over. will watch for 30m and then close if stable for 60m.

eng-oncall: monitoring dashboards — error rate for acme's tenant down to baseline. token throughput normalized.

ops-bot: Alert suppression: suppress similar websocket timeout alerts for tenant=acme for 10m while mitigation stabilizes.

julia (CSM): customer thanks the team and will await formal postmortem. they asked for timeline for a permanent fix (config + docs).

mike: create follow-up JIRA for infra to add per-tenant edge timeout and sticky-session defaults + docs for enterprise gateway configs. assign to eng-runtime.

eng-oncall: created jira INF-4321 "Per-tenant websocket timeout defaults + sticky routing" and linked incident r-78431.

eva: closing incident thread after 60m sustained stability. next steps: postmortem, RFO, include customer remediation checklist, include template NGINX snippet for keepalive/ping, and schedule a sync with Acme in 48h.

raj: thanks all. nice quick triage and good coordination with CSM.

eng-oncall: final status — mitigation applied, monitoring OK, handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
